ROLE: Answer whether a session pointer delivered by an epoll event is still a live registry entry, so an event for a session that was already reaped can never be dispatched into freed memory.

SIGNATURE.RAW: static int is_registered(const struct loop *l, const struct session *s)
SIGNATURE.NAME: is_registered

STRUCT.NAME: struct loop
STRUCT.ROLE: provides the borrowed broker whose registry is searched

STRUCT.NAME: struct broker
STRUCT.ROLE: owns the session registry that is the source of truth

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: pointer compared by identity, never dereferenced

FUNC.NAME: broker_session_count
FUNC.ROLE: size of the live registry scan

FUNC.NAME: broker_session_at
FUNC.ROLE: borrow each registry entry to compare pointers

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_session_count
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the number of sessions currently in the registry (0 for a NULL broker); the value is only a snapshot, it says nothing about the identity of the entries
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: read-only; no session is retained or modified
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; the result is used directly as the scan bound

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: broker_session_at
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: struct session *broker_session_at(const struct broker *b, size_t index)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the borrowed session stored at index, or NULL when index >= broker_session_count(b) or the broker is NULL
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: borrowed; the pointer stays valid only until the next broker_reap/broker_accept/broker_destroy, and this function only compares it
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: no failure under documented preconditions; a NULL result simply never compares equal to a session pointer that was passed in

LOGIC.INPUT: l: the loop whose broker registry is the authority (NULL tolerated). s: the session pointer carried by the epoll event data (NULL tolerated).
LOGIC.ACTION: 1. If l == NULL or s == NULL, return 0 (never trust an event without a pointer). 2. b = l->broker; if b == NULL return 0. 3. n = broker_session_count(b); loop i from 0 to n-1: if broker_session_at(b, i) == s, return 1. 4. Fall through and return 0: the pointer is not an entry of the current registry, which means the session was already destroyed by broker_reap (or by broker_destroy on the teardown path), so its memory may be reused and the event must be ignored.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: 1 when s is currently one of the broker's registry entries, 0 otherwise (including either argument being NULL).
INVARIANTS_USED: the broker registry is the single source of truth for live sessions
a session pointer is invalidated by broker_reap, so a pointer delivered with an event must be revalidated before use
reaping never happens inside a dispatched handler, so this guard is the only protection needed against a stale pointer from an earlier batch of the same epoll_wait call
the function never dereferences s, so a stale pointer cannot fault
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: l was created by loop_create and borrows a live broker, or is NULL.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: no state is modified; the registry and every session are untouched.

EXPECT.note: identity comparison against the registry, not a state test

runtime: create session S, close it by a DISCONNECT packet, broker_reap removes it
call is_registered(l, S) with the stale pointer, then feed a fabricated epoll event carrying it
